text: The primary goal of the Five Year Plans in India was to achieve:
explanation: The Five Year Plans in India were primarily aimed at achieving rapid economic growth. The First Five Year Plan (1951-1956) focused on increasing agricultural production and improving the standard of living of the people. The subsequent plans also emphasized on growth, modernisation, self-reliance, and equity.
subject: Economics

text: The Green Revolution in India was initiated to:
explanation: The Green Revolution in India was initiated in the 1960s to increase agricultural production and reduce dependence on food imports. The introduction of high-yielding varieties of wheat and other crops led to a significant increase in food production.
subject: Economics

text: The Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 (IPR 1956) aimed to:
explanation: The Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 (IPR 1956) aimed to promote import substitution and reduce dependence on foreign goods. The policy encouraged the growth of domestic industries and promoted self-reliance.
subject: Economics

text: The Land Reforms in India aimed to:
options: Increase land ownership among the rich
Reduce land ownership among the poor
Promote land redistribution among the poor
correctAnswer: Promote land redistribution among the poor
explanation: The Land Reforms in India aimed to promote land redistribution among the poor and reduce inequality in land ownership. The reforms aimed to increase the ownership of land among the marginalized sections of society.
subject: Economics

text: The Five Year Plans in India were criticized for:
explanation: The Five Year Plans in India were criticized for failing to address poverty and inequality. Despite rapid economic growth, the plans failed to reduce poverty and improve the standard of living of the marginalized sections of society.
subject: Economics

text: The Green Revolution in India led to:
options: Increased dependence on foreign food imports
explanation: The Green Revolution in India led to increased dependence on foreign fertilizers and other inputs. The introduction of high-yielding varieties of crops required the use of fertilizers and other inputs, which were often imported from abroad.

text: The Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 (IPR 1956) led to:
explanation: The Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 (IPR 1956) led to increased public sector participation in key industries. The policy encouraged the growth of public sector enterprises and promoted self-reliance.

text: The Five Year Plans in India were based on:
explanation: The Five Year Plans in India were based on the Lewis model, which emphasized the importance of labor absorption in the growth process. The model was used to estimate the potential for growth in the Indian economy.
